title: Where to Eat in KL on Your First Night
metaDescription: Looking for the best food in KL on your first night? Where to eat near KL Sentral, Bukit Bintang and Chinatown after the bus from KLIA2.

contentBlocks.content: Searching for the best food in KL before you land? Start with where your airport bus stops, because on your first night you want dinner close to your bed. This guide covers the three bus stops in the city from KLIA2: KL Sentral, Lalaport BBCC in Bukit Bintang, and Pudu Sentral by Chinatown. For each one you get what to eat nearby and how to reach it, plus two late places further out if you land after the malls close. The places come from the Teeko restaurant directory.
Key Takeaways

Which bus stop is closest to food? Each has dinner within one train ride or a walk. Lalaport BBCC is two Monorail stops from Bukit Bintang and Jalan Alor. Pudu Sentral is a walk from Petaling Street. KL Sentral has the NU Sentral mall next door.
Where do I eat if I land late? Jalan Alor fills up at night (Tourism Malaysia). Mee Tarik Restoran on Jalan Sultan in Chinatown often stays open until 6am, according to its listing.
Is the food halal? It depends on the place. Jalan Alor is mixed. Ask each place, or look for a halal certificate at the counter.
Is there plant-based food in Chinatown? Yes. The Hungry Tapir on Jalan Petaling cooks only with plants and has a full bar.
How do I get from KLIA2 to dinner? Book the bus to the stop nearest your hotel. Every route leaves from the Transportation Hub on Level 1 of KLIA2 (ttklia.com).
Landing at KL Sentral

The bus from KLIA2 to KL Sentral ends at KL Sentral itself (ttklia.com). If you are tired, eat next door. NU Sentral, at 201 Jalan Tun Sambanthan, lists food and beverage outlets in its store directory and opens 10am to 10pm daily (NU Sentral). If you land after about 9pm, the mall will be closing by the time you arrive, so head out instead.

For street food, Chinatown is one stop away. Take the LRT Kelana Jaya Line from KL Sentral to Pasar Seni, the next station, which is by Central Market and Petaling Street (klia2.info). For Bukit Bintang, take the KL Monorail from KL Sentral five stops to Bukit Bintang station (klia2.info).
Check in, leave your bags, then take one train to dinner. The KLIA2 to KL Sentral guide compares the bus, the train and the taxi.
Landing at Lalaport BBCC: Bukit Bintang

The bus to Lalaport BBCC ends at the transport hub on the lower ground floor of LaLaport Bukit Bintang City Centre. The hub is open 24 hours and connects to the LRT and Monorail at Hang Tuah. In the mall you will find ramen, Japanese curry and Korean barbecue buffet restaurants, and a CU convenience store with drinks and hot food (The Straits Times). The hub never closes but the mall restaurants do, so a late arrival means eating elsewhere.

From Hang Tuah, the Monorail runs two stops, through Imbi, to Bukit Bintang (klia2.info). Jalan Alor is the street food lane there, lined with seafood restaurants, hawker stalls and coffee shops, and it comes alive once night falls (Tourism Malaysia).
Meng Kee Grill Fish is on Jalan Alor itself. It grills seafood over an open flame and suits a late meal with a cold drink.

Rather eat in air conditioning? Pavilion Kuala Lumpur has Food Republic, a food court on Level 1 of the Gourmet Emporium, and Lot 10 Hutong is a hawker hall in the basement of Lot 10 (Tourism Malaysia). For Jalan Alor stall by stall, read the Jalan Alor food guide. For the rest of the area, see Bukit Bintang food.

From Bukit Bintang station it is about 1km along an air-conditioned route to the Petronas Twin Towers in KLCC (The Straits Times). Not A Ramen is a ramen counter in the Signature Food Court on Level 2 of the towers.
Staying in Bukit Bintang? Book the bus from KLIA2 to Lalaport BBCC, then walk to Jalan Alor for dinner. The KLIA2 to Bukit Bintang guide has every other way in.
Landing at Pudu Sentral: Chinatown
ttklia.com lists this route as KL City Centre (Pudu Sentral). Pudu Sentral is on the walk from Plaza Rakyat LRT station to Petaling Street, about 1km in all (klia2.info).

Petaling Street has plenty of Chinese food, hawker stalls and restaurants, with halal and non-halal places side by side. Tourism Malaysia gives the street market's hours as 8am to 8pm Sunday to Friday and 8am to 10pm on Saturday (Tourism Malaysia). Arrive after that and the market stalls are packing up, though restaurants keep their own hours.

Mee Tarik Restoran is on Jalan Sultan. It pulls its own noodles by hand and serves curry noodle bowls and noodle soups. Its listing says it often stays open until 6am, which helps after a late flight. If you eat halal, ask at the counter and look for a certificate before you order.
The Hungry Tapir is at 135 Jalan Petaling. It serves plant-based sharing plates, East meets West, with a full bar. It is dog friendly and takes larger groups.
Staying in Chinatown? Book the bus from KLIA2 to Pudu Sentral, drop your bags, then walk to Jalan Sultan or Jalan Petaling for dinner.
Landing late: food further out
If you land late and your hotel is outside the centre, a taxi or Grab can stop at a supper place on the way. These two are local supper spots, away from the tourist streets.
Restaurant Yan Yang A One is on Old Klang Road. It serves Chinese-style supper: deep-fried pork ribs, braised dishes and strong aromatics. Pork is on the menu, so it is not halal.
Nasi Lemak Burung Hantu TTDI is on Lorong Rahim Kajai 14. It serves coconut rice and sambal with fried chicken or egg, and its listing says the second branch often stays open even later.
For more late kitchens, use the supper in Kuala Lumpur guide. Eating halal? The halal ramen guide lists ramen shops in KL with halal certification.

contentBlocks.content: Frequently Asked Questions
Where should I eat on my first night in KL?

Eat near where your bus from KLIA2 stops. From Lalaport BBCC, take the Monorail two stops to Bukit Bintang for Jalan Alor. From Pudu Sentral, walk to Petaling Street and Jalan Sultan in Chinatown. From KL Sentral, eat at NU Sentral before 10pm or ride one LRT stop to Pasar Seni.
What is open late near KL Sentral?
NU Sentral, next to KL Sentral, opens 10am to 10pm daily (NU Sentral). After that, ride the LRT one stop to Pasar Seni for Chinatown, or check the supper guide.
Is Jalan Alor halal?
Jalan Alor is not halal as a whole. Some stalls serve pork and some do not, so ask at each stall or look for a halal certificate before you order.
Can I eat at Lalaport BBCC after a late bus?

The Lalaport transport hub is open 24 hours, but the mall's restaurants close at night. The CU convenience store in the mall sells drinks and hot food (The Straits Times). After the mall closes, take a Grab to a supper spot.
How far is Petaling Street from Pudu Sentral?
Petaling Street is a short walk from Pudu Sentral. klia2.info puts the walk from Plaza Rakyat LRT, past Pudu Sentral, to Petaling Street at about 1km (klia2.info).
Conclusion

Your first dinner in KL depends on where your bus stops. Lalaport BBCC is closest to Jalan Alor and Bukit Bintang. Pudu Sentral puts you on foot in Chinatown. KL Sentral has NU Sentral next door and one train to either area. Pick the stop nearest your hotel, then book your KLIA2 to KL Sentral bus on ttklia.com.
